nodes.content: Enable long-document reasoning that resolves conflicting, temporally scoped claims while preserving auditable evidence for multi-hop conclusions.
requirements: Exceed a matched-context retrieval baseline by 10 percentage points in conflicting-evidence question accuracy.
At least 90% of correct answers include complete, noncontradictory evidence chains respecting temporal scope.

nodes.content: Build versioned claim graphs with validity intervals, source-level provenance, contradiction edges, and constrained search yielding temporally consistent evidence chains.
How can versioned claim graphs distinguish superseding updates from genuine contradictions when reported validity intervals overlap?
Publication-time ordering and explicit correction links reduce overlap-label error by at least 20% versus interval-only labeling on TempoConflict.
Annotate TempoConflict overlapping claims, classify correction links and publication order, then compare overlap-label error against interval-only labeling.
Annotate 600 overlapping TempoConflict claim pairs; compare publication-order-and-correction versus interval-only classifiers on overlap-label error.
On 600 TempoConflict pairs, publication-order-and-correction labeling reduced overlap-label error from 24% to 16% versus interval-only labeling.
Audit the 96 remaining TempoConflict errors, distinguishing missing correction cues, disputed publication dates, and genuine simultaneous conflicts.
TempoConflict error ledger containing 96 audited pairs, categorized failure tags, disputed date records, and source-linked adjudications.
Independently audit 96 TempoConflict ledger adjudications for tag agreement; benchmark claim-graph search against matched-context retrieval for accuracy and chain completeness.
On TempoConflict, claim-graph accuracy reached 71% versus matched-context retrieval's 64%; 87% of correct answers had complete, noncontradictory temporal chains.
Keep correction-aware labeling (16% error), but defer deployment: graph search gains only 7 points and reaches 87% chain completeness.
Are missing cross-document entity-alias links responsible for most correct TempoConflict answers lacking complete, noncontradictory temporal evidence chains?
Audit incomplete chains from correct TempoConflict graph-search answers, restore verified cross-document aliases, and measure recovered complete-chain rate.
Of 100 incomplete TempoConflict chains, 62 lacked aliases; restoration completed 49, raising correct-answer chain completeness from 87% to 93%.
AliasTrace reranks multi-hop candidates by verified entity aliases, correction precedence, and interval entailment, then emits source-linked chains.
Implement AliasTrace; tune on TempoConflict development data; compare held-out accuracy with matched-context retrieval and audit correct-answer chain completeness.
Use TempoConflict's 96-pair adjudication ledger to implement AliasTrace correction and date checks, then tune alias-aware reranking on development questions.
AliasTrace v0.1: tuned reranker with verified-alias tables, correction-aware interval checks, and source-linked chain export.
Does AliasTrace v0.1 merge distinct entities sharing an alias across different validity periods, creating invalid evidence chains?
Excluding suspected cross-period entity merges should preserve at least 40 of 49 chains restored through verified aliases.
Adjudicate all 49 alias-restored chains for cross-period entity collisions; exclude suspect merges in AliasTrace v0.1 and count retained valid chains.
Of 49 alias-restored chains, 13 contained cross-period entity merges; filtering retained 36 valid chains, below the hypothesized 40.
Time-bounded aliases with canonical-ID checks will prevent at least 10/13 cross-period merges while retaining at least 34/36 valid chains.
Apply time-bounded aliases and canonical-ID checks to 13 merge cases and 36 valid chains; measure prevented merges and retained chains.
Time-bounded aliases and canonical-ID checks prevented 12/13 cross-period merges while retaining 35/36 previously valid chains.
Adopt time-bounded aliases in AliasTrace: of 49 restored chains, checks prevented 12/13 merges and retained 35/36 valid chains.
Compare original claim-graph search, time-bounded AliasTrace v0.1, and matched-context retrieval on held-out TempoConflict accuracy and correct-answer chain completeness.
Held-out TempoConflict: AliasTrace-enhanced claim-graph accuracy was 77%, original 71%, retrieval 64%; 92% of correct answers had complete, noncontradictory temporal chains.
Stress-test time-bounded AliasTrace v0.1 on TemporalShift-200 reused-alias corrections; audit answer accuracy, temporal-chain validity, and source-link integrity.
On TemporalShift-200, AliasTrace accuracy was 74% versus retrieval's 67%; only 82% of correct answers had complete, noncontradictory temporal chains.
Defer deployment: TempoConflict meets both targets (77% versus 64%, 92% chains), but TemporalShift-200 fails (74% versus 67%, 82%).
Introduce ScopeProof, a query-time proof checker that expands correction evidence and backtracks over invalid reused-alias joins.
Which TemporalShift-200 failures arise from missing correction evidence rather than reused-alias joins that ScopeProof can backtrack?
Missing correction evidence accounts for at least half of TemporalShift-200's incomplete correct-answer chains; reused-alias joins account for under one-third.
Audit TemporalShift-200 incomplete chains by failure cause, then implement ScopeProof correction expansion and alias backtracking against held-out retrieval.
Audit 27 incomplete TemporalShift-200 correct-answer chains, adjudicating missing correction evidence versus reused-alias joins against source documents.
TemporalShift-200 failure ledger: 27 source-linked incomplete-chain records with correction-missing, reused-alias, and other-cause adjudications.
Independently verify 27 ledger adjudications, estimate missing-correction and reused-alias fractions, and benchmark ScopeProof against AliasTrace on TemporalShift-200.
TemporalShift-200: 16/27 chains lacked corrections, 7/27 had alias errors; ScopeProof reached 79% accuracy and 91% correct-answer chain completeness.
Ablate ScopeProof correction expansion and alias backtracking separately on 27 ledger cases; compare chain repairs by adjudicated cause.
ScopeProof ablations found six correction-tagged chains repaired only by alias backtracking; revised causes: 10/27 missing corrections, 13/27 alias errors.
Prioritize alias backtracking while retaining correction expansion: revised failures favor aliases 13 to 10; ScopeProof achieved 79% accuracy, 91% chains.
On new TemporalShift-200 variants, reused-alias joins will exceed missing corrections among incomplete chains, accounting for at least 40%.
Generate held-out TemporalShift-200 variants with reused aliases and corrections; adjudicate incomplete chains and compare alias-error versus missing-correction shares.
Using ablation-revised cause labels, generate 120 held-out TemporalShift-200 variants and adjudicate incomplete ScopeProof chains for alias errors versus missing corrections.
Of 24 incomplete correct-answer chains across 120 held-out TemporalShift-200 variants, 11 (46%) involved alias errors versus eight missing corrections.
Re-adjudicate e10’s 24 incomplete chains using e9’s revised cause taxonomy; independently label failure causes and recalculate alias-error prevalence.
Independent re-adjudication reclassified two chains: alias errors were 9/24 (38%), below missing corrections at 10/24.
Retain both ScopeProof repairs without alias priority: independent review reversed alias-versus-correction counts from 11–8 to 9–10.
Develop TwinScope, a joint correction-and-alias proof search that validates temporal joins and exports minimal, source-linked evidence chains.
Can TwinScope jointly resolve correction precedence and reused aliases without pruning valid multi-hop chains under a fixed retrieval budget?
With 32 retrieved passages, TwinScope retains ≥95% of oracle-valid chains and achieves ≥80% accuracy and ≥93% chain completeness on TemporalShift-200.
Implement TwinScope under a 32-passage cap, annotate oracle-valid chains, then benchmark chain retention, accuracy, and completeness against ScopeProof and retrieval.
Implement TwinScope atop AliasTrace v0.1, using the TemporalShift failure ledger and re-adjudicated labels to tune 32-passage joint proof search.
TwinScope v0.1: 32-passage joint proof-search implementation with correction precedence, time-bounded alias validation, and minimal source-linked chain export.
Annotate oracle chains for TemporalShift-200; benchmark TwinScope v0.1 against ScopeProof and matched-context retrieval at 32 passages.
TemporalShift-200, 32 passages: TwinScope retained 96% oracle-valid chains, reached 82% accuracy (ScopeProof 79%, retrieval 67%), and 94% correct-answer chain completeness.
Stress-test TwinScope v0.1 at 32 passages on 120 unseen TemporalShift variants, measuring oracle-chain retention, accuracy, and temporal-chain completeness.
On 120 TemporalShift-200 variants at 32 passages, TwinScope retained 92% oracle chains, reached 79% accuracy and 89% correct-answer chain completeness.
Defer TwinScope deployment: TemporalShift-200 met targets, but unseen variants fell to 79% accuracy, 89% chain completeness, and 92% retention.
At 32 passages, correction-and-alias-aware selection will restore ≥95% oracle-chain retention and ≥90% chain completeness on unseen variants.
Add correction-and-alias-aware passage selection to TwinScope; compare oracle-chain retention, accuracy, and completeness on held-out variants at 32 passages.
Using e13’s failed variants, rerank passages by correction and alias links; measure chain retention and completeness under 32-passage cap.
On 120 unseen variants, correction-and-alias-aware selection raised oracle-chain retention from 92% to 96% and correct-answer completeness from 89% to 92%.
Freeze link-aware selection; compare enhanced versus original TwinScope v0.1 on 150 fresh variants for 32-passage retention and completeness.
On 150 fresh variants, link-aware TwinScope retained 93% oracle chains and reached 88% correct-answer chain completeness at 32 passages.
Defer link-aware TwinScope deployment: initial 96% retention and 92% completeness fell to 93% and 88% on fresh variants.
Given link-aware selection's 93% retention, diversity-constrained 32-passage coverage will reach ≥95% oracle-chain retention and ≥90% completeness on fresh variants.
Select 32 passages using source-date diversity constraints, then evaluate oracle-chain retention, accuracy, and completeness on untouched TemporalShift variants.
Implement source-date-diverse passage selection in TwinScope v0.1, reserving slots for corrections and distinct alias periods within 32 passages.
TwinScope v0.2 replaces v0.1's selector with 32-passage source-date-diverse coverage reserving correction and distinct alias-period evidence.
Benchmark TwinScope v0.2 on 200 untouched TemporalShift variants at 32 passages, auditing oracle-chain retention, accuracy, and correct-answer completeness.
On 200 untouched variants, TwinScope v0.2 achieved 79% accuracy, 94% oracle-chain retention, and 89% correct-answer chain completeness.
Audit v0.2’s missed oracle chains and incomplete answers, testing whether reserved correction and alias-period slots displaced required evidence.
Among 40 correction-heavy cases, v0.2 retained 39 oracle chains with 93% correct-answer completeness; reserved slots displaced none.
Stratify the remaining 160 variants by correction density and alias reuse; audit v0.2 chain omissions behind the subgroup–aggregate gap.
TwinScope v0.3 replaces fixed passage quotas with correction-density- and alias-reuse-adaptive selection informed by stratified omission audits.
Test TwinScope v0.3 on 250 new TemporalShift variants at 32 passages, comparing retention and completeness against v0.2 across correction-density strata.
On 250 new variants, TwinScope v0.3 retained 96% oracle chains and achieved 91% correct-answer completeness, versus v0.2’s 94% and 89%.
Advance v0.3 to stratified accuracy validation, not deployment: adaptive selection yields 96% retention and 91% completeness despite v0.2’s shortfall.
